New hoeing robot benefits from growers’ critical eye

 19-10 | Smart farming | Article

LinkedInFacebookXWhatsAppPrint

Ted and Nicoline Vaalburg invested at the beginning of 2026 in a Farming GT hoeing robot for their organic celeriac and pumpkins. The Farming GT is a 4- or 6-row, 4-wheel-drive, 4-wheel-steered hybrid tool carrier that can hoe both between and in the row. Photos: Mark Pasveer

The Farming GT hoeing robot cannot be accused of lacking experience. Originating from, among others, Amazone and Bosch, the vehicle has strong credentials from the outset. That is no guarantee of success here. A first impression underlines the importance of local support and a critical eye. You can have an affinity with it or not, but the fact is that the development and introduction of weed control robots is moving faster than that of many other machines.
